title: Chicken Korma
subtitle: Mild, creamy Indian chicken curry with almonds and coconut
excerpt: Tender chicken in a rich, mildly spiced sauce of onions, almonds, coconut milk, and cream. One of the best-loved Indian restaurant dishes, now easy to make at home.

recipe.sourceNotes: Korma is a style of curry rather than a specific recipe, originating in the Mughal courts of northern India in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The word korma (or qorma) comes from the Urdu and means 'braising': the technique of gently braising meat in its own juices or in a small amount of liquid rather than in a large quantity of sauce. The British restaurant version, introduced via the Bangladeshi restaurant trade in the 1970s and 1980s, is considerably milder and creamier than most traditional kormas, reflecting British taste preferences. It became the most popular curry in British restaurants and takeaways. Ground almonds are characteristic: they thicken the sauce and give it a nutty richness. The coconut milk version is a slightly later development and is now standard in British restaurant versions.

content.text: Fry the onion until deeply golden before adding the spices: this caramelisation is what gives the sauce its colour and sweetness. The onion must be cooked slowly over medium-low heat for at least 20 minutes; rushing this stage produces a raw, bitter-tasting sauce. Add the ground almonds with the yoghurt to help prevent the sauce from splitting.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the cardamom and cinnamon and fry for 30 seconds. Add the onion and cook for 20 to 25 minutes until deeply golden, stirring occasionally.
Add the garlic, ginger, coriander, cumin, and turmeric. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the chicken and stir to coat in the spices. Cook for 5 minutes until the chicken is sealed.

Stir in the yoghurt and ground almonds. Add the coconut milk and salt. Simmer gently for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. Stir in the cream and garam masala. Simmer for 5 more minutes. Scatter with coriander. Serve with rice or naan.
